subject: Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
practicalPaper: Paper 3 is a practical test of 3 hours 10 minutes with one compulsory question for 100 marks (a theoretical alternative may be set where materials cannot be acquired). Candidates typically repair and prepare a damaged panel and spray it, and are marked on correct tool use, metal finishing, filler and surface preparation, paint mixing, spraying technique, final appearance and safety.

practicals.title: Personal protective equipment and workshop housekeeping
practicals.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
practicals.aim: To identify and use body-shop PPE, handle hazardous waste correctly and keep the workshop safe.
materials: Labelled hazardous waste containers (solvents, paint sludge, rags)
Sawdust and dry sand for spills
safety: Isocyanate (2K) paints require an air-fed or properly fitted respirator — a dust mask is not enough.
No smoking or naked flames in the paint area.
No horse-play around tools, compressors and vehicles on stands.
procedure: Identify each PPE item and the hazard it controls (dust, fumes, noise, sparks, chemicals).
Fit and seal-check a respirator.
Clean an oil spill using sawdust or dry sand; dispose of it in the correct container.
Sort waste: used thinner (solvent recovery), paint residue, rags, metal scrap.
Inspect equipment; tag and report any faulty machine.
Check the location of extinguishers, first aid box and exits.
practicals.expectedObservations: Correct PPE is worn for each task; spills are cleaned promptly; waste is separated and labelled.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Solvent recovery: if a recycler recovers 80% of 25 L of used gun-wash thinner, 0.8 × 25 = 20 L can be reused, and only 5 L goes for hazardous disposal.
precautions: Replace respirator cartridges as scheduled.
Store flammables in a metal cabinet.
sourcesOfError: Poorly fitting respirators letting vapour in.
commonMistakes: Using a dust mask for spraying.
Pouring thinner into drains.
examTips: Group hazards by source: human factors, machinery, workshop keeping.
Mention environmental and hazardous-waste regulations in theory answers.

practicals.title: Identifying and using body repair hand and power tools
practicals.aim: To identify body repair hand tools, power tools and spray equipment, state their uses and demonstrate care and maintenance.
safety: Check air hoses and couplings before use.
Wear goggles and ear defenders with power tools.
procedure: Lay out tools and identify each by name.
State the use of each and group them as hand tools, power tools and spray tools.
Demonstrate correct hammer-and-dolly grip.
Drain moisture from the compressor tank and check the air filter.
Clean and oil tools after use; store them on a shadow board.
Record the maintenance schedule from the manufacturer's guide.
practicals.expectedObservations: Tools are correctly identified, used and maintained according to the guide.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Compressor check: a DA sander needs about 300 L/min of free air. A compressor delivering 250 L/min cannot run it continuously; a unit of at least 300–350 L/min is needed.
precautions: Keep hammer faces and dollies polished; marks transfer to the panel.
sourcesOfError: Using worn abrasive discs on power sanders.
commonMistakes: Using a hammer with a damaged face.
Leaving water in the compressor tank.
examTips: Classify maintenance: predictive, preventive, corrective, with examples.
Give advantages and disadvantages of machines.

practicals.title: Mixing and applying body filler
practicals.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
practicals.aim: To identify body fillers, abrasives and sealers and to mix and apply polyester filler to a shallow dent.
materials: Abrasive papers P80, P120, P180 (dry) and P400–P800 (wet and dry)
safety: Wear gloves and a dust mask; filler dust is harmful.
Hardener (peroxide) irritates skin and eyes.
procedure: Identify each material and its use.
Clean and grind the dent to bare metal, feathering 25–50 mm beyond.
Measure filler and add hardener at about 2% by weight; mix by folding (not whipping) until uniform colour.
Apply thin layers, pressing the first into the metal.
Shape with the body file at the "cheesy" stage.
Block sand with P80, then P120 and P180 to the panel contour.
Check with hand and eye; fill pinholes with a skim coat.
practicals.expectedObservations: The filler cures to a hard, smooth contour flush with the panel, without pinholes.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Hardener at 2% by weight: 100 g filler → 2 g hardener; 250 g filler → 5 g hardener. Too much hardener causes bleed-through staining; too little leaves soft, uncured filler.
precautions: Apply filler only on clean bare metal.
Keep filler thin — usually not more than about 3 mm.
commonMistakes: Whipping air into the filler (pinholes).
Applying filler over paint or rust.
examTips: Distinguish undercoats (primer, putty, sealer) from topcoats (enamel, lacquer).
State filler types: plastic, fibreglass, body solder (lead).

practicals.title: Identifying metals and demonstrating their properties
practicals.aim: To identify ferrous and non-ferrous metals used in vehicle bodies and demonstrate malleability, ductility and work-hardening.
materials: Samples: mild steel body panel, high-strength steel, cast iron, aluminium panel, brass, copper strip
safety: Wear goggles when bending or breaking samples.
Gloves for sharp edges.
procedure: Identify each sample by appearance and magnet test.
Bend a mild steel strip back and forth until it breaks, feeling it stiffen (work-hardening).
Hammer a copper strip to show malleability.
File each sample to compare hardness.
Strike cast iron gently to show brittleness.
Record properties and body uses.
practicals.expectedObservations: Steel and cast iron are magnetic; aluminium, copper and brass are not. Bent mild steel becomes harder near the bend; cast iron breaks rather than bends.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Weight saving: a steel bonnet skin (0.8 mm, 1.5 m², density 7 850 kg/m³) weighs 0.0008 × 1.5 × 7 850 = 9.4 kg; an aluminium skin of 1.2 mm (density 2 700 kg/m³) weighs 0.0012 × 1.5 × 2 700 = 4.9 kg.
precautions: Use small samples and steady force.
commonMistakes: Assuming all silver-coloured panels are steel.
examTips: Define fusibility, malleability, ductility, weldability.
State where each metal is used on a vehicle.

practicals.title: Heat treatment of body metals
practicals.aim: To demonstrate annealing, hardening and tempering, and to show how heat shrinking relieves stretched panel metal.
safety: Wear gas goggles, gloves and apron.
Keep a fire extinguisher at hand; remove flammables.
procedure: Anneal a work-hardened steel strip by heating to dull red and cooling slowly; bend to compare.
Harden a high-carbon strip by heating to cherry red and quenching; test with a file.
Temper the hardened strip to blue and compare toughness.
Heat-shrink a stretched (bulged) area: heat a small spot to cherry red, tap it down with hammer on dolly, then quench with a wet rag.
Repeat on adjacent spots until the panel is flat.
Record observations.
practicals.expectedObservations: Annealed steel bends easily; hardened steel is file-hard; heat-shrinking pulls the stretched bulge back level.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Shrinking spot size is about 10–20 mm diameter. A bulge 150 mm across may need 5–8 spots, working from the outside towards the centre.
precautions: Heat only small spots; large areas distort the panel.
Avoid heating near fuel tanks or interior trim.
sourcesOfError: Overheating causing burn-through on thin panels.
commonMistakes: Heating too large an area.
Quenching high-strength steels not designed for heat.
examTips: Define each heat treatment process with its purpose.
Explain why stretched metal needs shrinking.

practicals.title: Installing oxy-acetylene equipment and identifying weld defects
practicals.aim: To install oxy-acetylene equipment for a low-pressure system, select nozzles and identify defects in welded body panel samples.
safety: Secure cylinders upright; no oil on oxygen fittings.
Light acetylene first, shut it off first.
procedure: Fit regulators, arrestors and hoses; check thread directions and colours.
Leak-test joints with fluid.
Select a small nozzle for thin panel steel.
Light and set a neutral flame.
Run a short weld on sheet steel.
Examine samples for porosity, slag inclusion, cracks and lack of penetration; state remedies.
Shut down and bleed lines.
practicals.expectedObservations: A neutral flame gives a clean weld; defects show as holes, inclusions or cracks.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Nozzle selection guide (typical): size 1 for up to 0.9 mm, size 2 for 0.9–1.2 mm, size 3 for 1.2–2.0 mm steel. A 0.8 mm body panel therefore uses a size 1 nozzle.
precautions: Use the smallest suitable nozzle on body panels to limit distortion.
Tack weld at intervals.
commonMistakes: Long continuous welds on thin panels (warping).
examTips: Describe high- and low-pressure systems.
Table of weld defects and remedies.

practicals.title: Hammer and dolly repair of a minor dent
practicals.aim: To straighten a minor dent in a steel panel using hammer-on-dolly and hammer-off-dolly techniques and finish with a body file.
apparatus: Stud welder and slide hammer (for closed panels)
materials: Damaged steel door skin or wing
safety: Wear goggles and gloves.
Support the panel firmly.
procedure: Study the damage: identify direct damage, buckles and stretched areas.
Rough out the dent by pushing or pulling from behind (spoon/pry bar) or pull with a stud puller.
Use hammer-off-dolly to bring high spots down and low spots up together.
Use hammer-on-dolly to smooth and planish (careful: this stretches metal).
Apply guide coat and file lightly to show highs and lows.
Pick up lows and tap down highs until the panel is level.
Heat-shrink any stretched area.
practicals.expectedObservations: Filing shows an even bright surface with very few low spots; the panel contour matches the undamaged side.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Repair limit check: if the remaining low area after metal finishing is no deeper than about 3 mm, a thin skim of filler finishes it; deeper lows need more metal work.
precautions: Work the damage in reverse order of how it happened.
Use light, accurate blows.
commonMistakes: Hitting the panel hard without a dolly.
Using filler to cover large dents.
examTips: Explain hammer-on and hammer-off dolly techniques.
Identify integral and composite body types.

checkQuestions.explanation: The dolly is placed under the low spot beside the hammer blow.

practicals.title: Checking body alignment with a tram gauge
practicals.aim: To measure body diagonals with a tram gauge and identify misalignment in a damaged vehicle structure.
safety: Support the vehicle securely on stands.
Pulling equipment is operated only by trained staff with safety chains.
procedure: Identify the major body sections: front engine compartment, passenger section, rear section.
Locate reference holes from the dimension chart.
Measure X-diagonals in the engine compartment and underbody with the tram gauge.
Compare left and right diagonals and with the chart.
Identify the direction of misalignment (sway, sag, mash, twist, diamond).
Plan the straightening pull opposite to the direction of impact.
practicals.expectedObservations: Unequal diagonals reveal side sway or diamond damage; correct structures have matching diagonals within tolerance.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Underbody diagonals: 1 452 mm and 1 466 mm. Difference = 1 466 − 1 452 = 14 mm, much more than a typical 3 mm tolerance → the structure is out of alignment and must be pulled.
precautions: Measure from the same type of reference point on each side.
Keep the tram gauge pointers at equal heights.
sourcesOfError: Tram bar flex over long distances.
commonMistakes: Measuring to damaged reference holes.
examTips: Name the types of frame damage and state the basic alignment principle.
Describe quarter-panel cutting and light-weight panels in theory.

checkQuestions.explanation: A square structure has equal diagonals.

practicals.title: Repairing and aligning an aluminium panel
practicals.aim: To repair a dented aluminium panel using heat to soften it and suitable tools that avoid contamination.
apparatus: Dedicated aluminium hammers and dollies (or wooden/plastic mallets)
materials: Damaged aluminium panel (e.g. bonnet or deck lid)
safety: Aluminium does not glow before melting — use temperature crayons to avoid burning through.
Aluminium dust is flammable: separate it from steel dust and use extraction.
procedure: Clean the area with a stainless steel brush (never one used on steel).
Mark the area with temperature crayon and warm it gently (about 150–200 °C) to soften.
Rough out the dent with light blows from the back, using wooden or plastic tools.
Use hammer-off-dolly with care; aluminium work-hardens and cracks easily.
Pull closed sections with an aluminium stud welder.
Metal-finish carefully; avoid grinding through.
For a deck lid, remove fittings first and support it on a padded bench.
practicals.expectedObservations: The panel returns to shape without cracking when warmed; overworked areas become stiff and may crack.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Aluminium melts at about 660 °C compared with about 1 500 °C for steel, and conducts heat about three times better — so it reaches melting point quickly without changing colour.
precautions: Keep aluminium tools separate from steel tools (galvanic corrosion).
Use lighter blows than on steel.
commonMistakes: Using steel wire brushes.
Hitting hard and stretching the soft metal.
examTips: List the steps in aluminium panel repair.
Explain why steel contamination causes corrosion.

checkQuestions.q: Aluminium is warmed before straightening to
checkQuestions.explanation: Warm aluminium is less likely to crack.

practicals.title: Repairing a plastic bumper by plastic welding
practicals.aim: To identify a bumper plastic and repair a crack by melting (plastic welding) with matching filler rod.
safety: Ventilate; burning plastics give toxic fumes.
Wear gloves; welder tip is very hot.
procedure: Identify the plastic from the moulded code inside (e.g. >PP<, >ABS<, >PUR<).
Confirm it is a thermoplastic (can be re-melted).
Clean with plastic cleaner; V-groove the crack on both sides; drill a stop hole at its end.
Align the crack with aluminium tape on the face side.
Weld from the back with matching rod, fusing rod and base together.
Weld the face side; allow to cool naturally.
Sand flush; apply adhesion promoter and flexible filler/primer for painting.
practicals.expectedObservations: The rod fuses into the groove forming a continuous bead; after sanding, the repair is flush and flexible.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Crack 80 mm long with welds on both sides needs about 2 × 80 = 160 mm of bead; with a little extra for start and finish, cut about 200 mm of filler rod.
precautions: Match the rod to the plastic type.
Do not overheat (plastic chars and weakens).
sourcesOfError: Misidentified plastic giving a weak bond.
commonMistakes: Trying to weld a thermosetting plastic.
Painting without adhesion promoter.
examTips: Distinguish thermoplastics (re-meltable) and thermosets (not re-meltable).
Introduce glass-fibre panel repair.

practicals.title: Dismantling, cleaning and adjusting a spray gun
practicals.aim: To identify spray gun types and parts, dismantle and clean a gun, and adjust it for correct spray pattern.
apparatus: Air pressure gauge at the gun
safety: Disconnect the air supply before dismantling.
Clean guns in a ventilated area with gloves and goggles; never point a gun at anyone.
procedure: Identify the gun type by cup position: gravity (above), suction (below), pressure-feed (remote pot).
Name the parts: air cap, fluid tip (nozzle), fluid needle, air valve, trigger, fan control, fluid control, body, cup.
Dismantle air cap, fluid tip and needle; clean with brush and thinner (never soak the whole gun).
Lubricate needle packing and trigger pivot; reassemble.
Set the air pressure (per the gun data sheet) and test the fan pattern on paper.
Adjust fan width and fluid flow for an even oval pattern.
practicals.expectedObservations: A clean, well-adjusted gun gives an even elliptical pattern with uniform atomisation; a blocked air cap horn gives a crescent or heavy-sided pattern.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Gun-to-panel distance about 15–20 cm. If the fan is 200 mm wide and each pass overlaps 50%, the gun moves 100 mm down per pass: a 900 mm high door needs about 900/100 = 9 passes per coat.
precautions: Do not use metal wire to clean air cap holes.
Never immerse the whole gun in thinner (damages seals).
sourcesOfError: Incorrect air pressure for the gun type.
commonMistakes: Losing the needle packing.
Reassembling with the needle bent.
examTips: Compare gravity, suction and pressure-feed guns.
State precautions in using a spray gun.

practicals.title: Preparing a metal surface for spray painting
practicals.aim: To prepare a repaired panel for painting: cleaning, sanding, feather-edging, priming and masking.
materials: Abrasives P80, P180, P320, P400–P800 wet and dry
safety: Wear a dust mask when sanding and a respirator when spraying primer.
Use extraction or wet-sanding to control dust.
procedure: Wash the panel, then degrease with wax and grease remover.
Sand damaged paint back and feather-edge the paint layers over 25–50 mm.
Treat bare metal with etch or epoxy primer.
Apply primer surfacer in 2–3 coats with flash-off between.
When cured, apply guide coat and block sand with P400–P800 (wet) until smooth.
Degrease again, mask adjacent areas and tack-off dust.
practicals.expectedObservations: A uniform, smooth primer surface with no visible edges, scratches or contamination; guide coat removed evenly.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Abrasive sequence for primer: P320 then P400 (dry) or P600–P800 (wet). Each grade should remove the scratches of the previous grade; skipping from P80 to P400 leaves scratches that swell through the topcoat.
precautions: Degrease before sanding to avoid driving contamination into the surface.
Allow primer to cure fully before sanding.
sourcesOfError: Contamination with silicone causing fish-eyes later.
commonMistakes: Insufficient feather-edging (ring marks).
Touching the cleaned surface with bare hands.
examTips: List the preparation stages in order.
Explain feather-edging and guide coat.

practicals.title: Identifying paint types with the solvent test and paint code
practicals.aim: To identify whether an existing finish is lacquer (cellulose/acrylic) or enamel/2K by the solvent test, and to locate the manufacturer's paint code.
apparatus: Colour chart and paint mixing guide
materials: Panels finished in cellulose, synthetic enamel and 2K paint
safety: Thinner is flammable and harmful: gloves and ventilation.
procedure: Moisten a cloth with thinner and rub a hidden area of the finish for a few seconds.
Observe: colour on the cloth and softening indicates lacquer; no effect suggests cured enamel or 2K.
Locate the paint code plate (door pillar, engine bay, boot).
Use the code and colour chart to select the colour and variant.
Read the paint formula for the required quantity.
Record results.
practicals.expectedObservations: Cellulose lacquer dissolves and transfers colour to the cloth; 2K and cured enamels resist thinner.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: 2K topcoat mixed 4:1:1 by volume (paint : hardener : thinner): 600 mL paint needs 600/4 = 150 mL hardener and 150 mL thinner, giving 900 mL ready-to-spray.
precautions: Test in an inconspicuous place.
Use the paint code, not visual matching alone.
sourcesOfError: Faded paint differing from original code colour.
commonMistakes: Spraying cellulose over uncured enamel (lifting/wrinkling).
examTips: State the importance of the manufacturer's paint code.
Name paint types: cellulose, synthetic enamel, acrylic, 2K, metallic.

practicals.title: Spray painting a panel
practicals.aim: To apply a solid colour topcoat to a prepared panel with correct gun distance, speed, overlap and flash-off times.
safety: Respirator (air-fed for 2K), gloves, spray suit and goggles.
No sources of ignition; booth extraction on.
procedure: Mix paint to the formula and strain it into the gun.
Set pressure and test the pattern.
Tack the panel.
Spray edges and corners first.
Spray the face holding the gun square, 15–20 cm away, moving at steady speed with 50% overlap; trigger at each end.
Allow flash-off; apply further coats as specified.
Remove masking at the right time; allow to cure; inspect for runs, dry spray and orange peel.
practicals.expectedObservations: An even, glossy film without runs or dry spray; orange peel is minimal.
practicals.dataAndCalculations: Bonnet 1.2 m × 0.9 m = 1.08 m²; two coats = 2.16 m² of coverage. If ready-to-spray paint covers about 8 m² per litre per coat, paint needed = 2.16/8 = 0.27 L (mix about 0.3 L).
precautions: Keep the gun perpendicular and at constant distance.
Observe flash-off times between coats.
sourcesOfError: Temperature and humidity affecting flow and drying.
commonMistakes: Arcing the gun (uneven film).
Spraying too close (runs) or too far (dry spray).
examTips: Describe defects (runs, orange peel, dry spray, blushing) with causes and remedies.
Show the coverage calculation.

practicals.title: Metallic spray technique
practicals.aim: To spray a metallic basecoat and clear coat, controlling flake orientation by wet and dry (drop) coats.
safety: Respirator and full PPE; ventilated booth.
procedure: Stir the metallic basecoat thoroughly so flakes are evenly dispersed.
Make a spray-out card to check colour match.
Apply basecoat in medium-wet coats until hiding is achieved.
Apply a final light drop (dry) coat from slightly further away to even the flake.
Allow the basecoat to flash off matt.
Apply two coats of clear.
Compare face and side tone with the spray-out card.
practicals.expectedObservations: Wet coats make the colour darker on the face (flakes lie deeper); dry coats make it lighter (flakes near the surface). Uneven technique causes mottling (striping).
practicals.dataAndCalculations: If the basecoat needs 3 coats to hide and each uses about 0.1 L on a door, about 0.3 L of reduced basecoat is needed; with a 1:1 reduction, mix 0.15 L basecoat with 0.15 L thinner.
precautions: Keep constant gun distance and speed.
Stir frequently.
commonMistakes: Applying clear before the basecoat flashes off.
Not making a spray-out card.
examTips: Explain variable agents: flakes (aluminium, pearl/mica) and pigments.
Describe wet and dry spray techniques and their effects on colour.
